newsitem.title: JAPAN: Report says G7 to urge Japan to cut trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Report says G7 to urge Japan to cut trade surplus.

text.p: Leaders of the Group of Seven major industrialised nations will urge Japan to cut its trade surplus and push forward economic reforms at their meeting in Denver later this month, a Japanese newspaper said on Thursday.
The Yomiuri Shimbun quoted Japanese government sources as saying that the leaders of the G7 would make the request in an economic statement to be issued during the June 20-22 meeting.
The statement will specify macroeconomic policy targets for each country for the first time since the 1993 Tokyo summit, it added.
For the steadily growing economies of Canada and the United States, the joint statement will call for measures to prevent a rekindling of inflation as well as steps to establish sound finances.
The G7's European members -- Britain, France, Germany and Italy -- will be asked to create employment opportunities and to curb high unemployment rates through job market reforms, the newspaper said.
The statement will call on Japan to avert a surge in its trade surplus by achieving economic growth led by domestic demand, the Yomiuri said.
